articleText:
[Hacker News — github.com]
Break the 64 GB RAM Wall: Run 284B DeepSeek-V4-Flash (< 59 GiB RAM) & 30B MoEs (up to 111 tok/s) at 256K Context on Pure CPU — Zero GPUs Required.

⚡ Quickstart · 🧩 Supported Models · 🖥️ Supported Chips & Platforms · 🏆 Leaderboard · 📄 Preprint PDF ( paper/ ) · 📐 Architecture · ❓ FAQ

Real-time Frontier & Agentic MoE inference on the CPU workstation you already own — 100% in RAM, zero NVMe swap:

🐧 Linux & 🍎 macOS (1-Command Automated Setup & Chat) git clone https://github.com/synchopate/llama-modchip.git cd llama-modchip ./modchip chat ⚡ Zero-Compile Direct Run (Pre-Compiled Linux x86_64 Binary + Hugging Face .gguf ) ⚠️ Important Compatibility Note ( GGML_TYPE_Q2_0 = 40 ): Our Fractal-64 models use custom block-64 BF16 -scale Gray-coded tensors ( GGML_TYPE_Q2_0 , type ID 40 ) and custom deepseek4 / Stockfish-PVS kernels. Opening them in unpatched llama.cpp , Ollama, or LM Studio will fail with unknown tensor type 40 . Use either ./modchip above or our standalone single-file pre-compiled binary ( llama-server-modchip-linux-x86_64 , zero .so dependencies) bundled directly inside the Hugging Face repositories and GitHub Release v2.4.0 :

# 1. For 30B Nemotron-3.5-A3B (14.35 GiB — runs in 16–32 GB RAM at 25–60.4 tok/s): hf download Synchopate/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B-Fractal-64-CPU-GGUF \ llama-server-modchip-linux-x86_64 NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B-Fractal-64.gguf --local-dir . chmod +x llama-server-modchip-linux-x86_64 ./llama-server-modchip-linux-x86_64 -m NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B-Fractal-64.gguf -c 262144 -t 16 --port 8080 # 2. For 284B DeepSeek-V4-Flash (56.56 GiB — fits in 64 GB RAM at 9.1–14.7 tok/s): hf download Synchopate/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Fractal-64GB-CPU-GGUF --local-dir ./dsv4 chmod +x ./dsv4/llama-server-modchip-linux-x86_64 ./dsv4/llama-server-modchip-linux-x86_64 -m ./dsv4/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Fractal-00001-of-00003.gguf -c 32768 -t 16 -fa on --port 8080 🪟 Windows 10/11 (1-Click Hybrid GPU + CPU MoE Pack) Open windows/ and double-click windows/AVVIA_MODCHIP.bat (or run ./modchip start in Git Bash). It automatically detects your CPU cores, free RAM, and GPU VRAM ( nvidia-smi ), downloads official llama.cpp CUDA 12.4 / Vulkan binaries, computes the optimal --n-cpu-moe split, and opens the Web Chat UI ( http://127.0.0.1:8080 ).

curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/synchopate/llama-modchip/main/scripts/check_cpu_readiness.py | python3 👉 Paste your terminal scorecard in a 📊 1-Click GitHub Benchmark Issue or GitHub Discussions to be added to the Official Community CPU Leaderboard!

Each model family has a dedicated deep-dive optimization guide with exact mathematical proofs, operator-level latency breakdowns, and quality gate benchmarks:

Full microarchitectural details and tuning flags for every supported processor and GPU hybrid are documented in docs/HARDWARE_OPTIMIZATIONS.md :

1. DeepSeek-V4-Flash 284B ( 13.17B Active) on a 64 GB Zen 5 CPU ( AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX , 0 GPUs ) Full operator-level profiling and mathematical proofs in docs/DEEPSEEK_V4_OPTIMIZATIONS.md :

Full ablation tables and 100/100 Quality Gate report in docs/NEMOTRON_OPTIMIZATIONS.md :

Run ./modchip bench (or windows\BENCHMARK_PC.bat on Windows) and ➕ Submit Your Scorecard (1-Click GitHub Issue) !

llama-modchip/ ├── modchip # Unified CLI (setup | start | chat | bench | eval | quantize | web | claude | stop) ├── install.sh # 1-Command Automated Installer (Linux) ├── README.md / ARCHITECTURE.md / FAQ.md # Clean Overview, Full Mathematical Paper & Engineering FAQ ├── RELEASE_NOTES.md # v2.4.0 Release Notes ├── docs/ │ ├── NEMOTRON_OPTIMIZATIONS.md # Deep-dive on Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B & Nemotron-H-8B optimizations │ ├── DEEPSEEK_V4_OPTIMIZATIONS.md # Deep-dive on DeepSeek-V4-Flash 284B profiling, SVD & L2-quadrature MoE │ └── HARDWARE_OPTIMIZATIONS.md # Chip-by-chip optimizations (Zen 5, Threadripper, Vulkan, CUDA, Metal, ARM64) ├── patches/ │ ├── deepseek-v4-flash-fractal-256k.patch # Unified v2.4.0 patch (DeepSeek-V4-Flash 284B + Nemotron-3.5 30B, Linux/macOS/Windows) │ └── zen5-nemotron-256k-optimizations.patch # Standalone ggml/llama core patch for Nemotron-3.5 ├── windows/ # 1-Click Windows 10/11 Hybrid GPU+CPU MoE Pack (AVVIA_MODCHIP.bat, modchip_win.ps1) ├── apple-silicon/ # Apple M4 Pro (24 GB) Metal setup & 128K benchmarks ├── fedora/ # Fedora 44 / AMD Ryzen 7 8745HS (GEEKOM A8) all-in-one script ├── speculative/ # RouteCrack + Stockfish-PVS v2 (rc_stockfish.h, ngram-map.cpp, 96+ techniques) ├── benchmarks/ # eval_quality_and_tools.py (100-pt Quality Gate) & results/*.json ├── gateway/sse_gateway.py # Agentic SSE Proxy + Compact Tool Table + Dark-Mode Web Chat HUD (:8787) └── scripts/ # build_fractal_moe_gguf.sh, transcode_dsv4.{c,py}, chat.py, llama_modchip.py 🏢 Enterprise & Hardware Sponsorships llama-modchip demonstrates that modern multi-core CPUs and compact Mini-PCs with 64–128 GB of DDR5 RAM can run 284B Frontier MoEs ( DeepSeek-V4-Flash ) and 30B Hybrid MoEs ( Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B ) local
reactions: [Hacker News] Everyone else, yes. This one is particularly mindbendingly bad. It is almost not human-readable without LLM summary.

[Hacker News] hm... this is the first time. TIL something from the HN comments more than the actual article. I'm relatively new to the AI space and the idea of quantization is something I'll have to take forward when evaluating future models.
[Hacker News] Deepseek v4 flash 0731 in a 2-bit quant has been useful for me. Other models don't seem to hold up nearly as well at 2-bit. Most of my other models are 5-6 bit quants because of this.
[Hacker News] This is a very impressive achievement in an unexpected direction. I'm really looking forward to trying out qwen on this system.

[Hacker News] I use lemonade llama.cpp with a 2-bit quant of DeepseekV4F 0731 that runs at about 15 tokens a second. I use it as my "smol" model in omp, with default going to OpenCode hosted Deepseek (faster inference). I haven't done work lately on Dwarf Star. I got it running a few weeks ago and had my agent make a couple of modifications to it to get it running, but it wasn't materially b

[Hacker News] Ironically, local models are much more efficient when running multiple parallel agents, provided that KV storage requirements are not excessive (not an issue with DeepSeek 4.1 Flash). It does not make any individual agent faster, but it does raise overall throughput quite a bit. The limit is then set by compute constraints rather than memory bandwidth, so something like DGX Spark or AMD Strix&#x2F
